territorial_scope.description: Applies to US federal agencies and to awardees of federal AI institute funding, which must be based in the United States.

evidence.quote: No funds authorized in this title shall be awarded to Institutes outside of the United States.

summary.short: Establishes a federal National Artificial Intelligence Initiative with coordinating offices, committees, a NIST standards mandate, research institutes and agency R&D programs. Its duties fall mainly on federal agencies and grant recipients; the NIST risk management framework is voluntary.
summary.long: Division E of the FY2021 National Defense Authorization Act (Pub. L. 116-283) establishes a National Artificial Intelligence Initiative, defines artificial intelligence and machine learning, and directs federal agencies to coordinate AI research, development, education and workforce activities. It creates a National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Office under the Office of Science and Technology Policy, an Interagency Committee to prepare a strategic plan within two years, and a National Artificial Intelligence Advisory Committee under the Secretary of Commerce. It establishes a workforce study by the National Academies, a National AI Research Resource Task Force, and an NSF-led program of financial assistance for AI research institutes limited to US-based awardees. Section 22A of the NIST Act directs NIST to develop a voluntary risk management framework within two years, support standards, and issue dataset documentation and data-sharing guidance. It also sets up a NOAA AI Center, NSF research and education grants with an ethics-statement report, and a DOE AI research program, with authorized appropriations for each. The Initiative terminates ten years after enactment; the text contains no penalties or private-sector mandates.

thresholds.note: The instrument is a research, funding and coordination statute. Its numbers are appropriation amounts (Secs. 5301(g), 5303(f), 5401(g), 5501(k)), fiscal-year and calendar deadlines, a 10-year sunset (Sec. 5101(e)), a 12-member Task Force composition (Sec. 5106(a)(2)), and 5-year award periods (Sec. 5201(b)(4)). None sets a cutoff that changes the legal treatment of a person or entity, so none is coded as a threshold.
